chunks: Moses said: "I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every insolent imposter who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning."

key_terms.مُتَكَبِّرٍ: The arrogant, one who is conceited and looks down on others
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ: The Day of Reckoning, when deeds are judged

ai.seo_question: What does Moses seek refuge from in this verse?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Ghafir, Prophet Moses (AS) invokes God's protection from those who, like Pharaoh, exhibit *takabbur* (arrogant pride) that blinds them to the reality of the Day of Judgment. Shia scholarship often contrasts this specific arrogance with the humility of the *Ahl al-Bayt*, viewing the rejection of divine truth by the elite as a recurring historical pattern. This highlights the spiritual danger of pride, which severs the connection between the believer and the accountability of the Hereafter.
